Triage: lands in `packages/services/service-datasource` (`external-datasource-service.ts` reads `col.primaryKey`; the driver emits `isPrimary`) ⇒ `pm:queue` · `domain:services` · type Bug. Rationale: every SQL driver's introspected PK is silently dropped from the generated federated object — measured twice, confirmed in shipped `dist`, and the existing pin feeds a hand-written fake so it can't see it.

Dispatch notes:
- Preferred fix at the seam: fall back to `table.primaryKeys?.includes(col.name)` (authoritative), with `col.primaryKey ?? col.isPrimary` as the per-column read; REQUIRED: a pin that drives `generateObjectDraft` off a **real** `SqlDriver.introspectSchema()` result.
- **Contract-spelling unification is not this card**: the two `IntrospectedColumn` declarations (`packages/objectql/src/util.ts:20` vs `packages/spec/src/contracts/schema-diff-service.ts:59`) disagreeing is the root — but anything touching `packages/spec` belongs to the spec seat. If you conclude the spec contract itself should change spelling, stop at the seam fix here and report it as an out-of-scope finding for spec routing; do not edit `packages/spec` in this PR.
- Sibling: #10712 (draft also fails `os build` — namespace prefix + `sharingModel`) is the same generator; if one dev takes both, answer the family-dispatch five gates at claim time.

Size/model suggestion: M, opus floor.

- worktree: `../objectstack-10676`
- Clause-②: **no** — argued, not assumed. The response *shape* of `POST /api/v1/datasources/*/object-draft` does not change; a field that should always have carried `primaryKey: true` starts carrying it. That is the same "contract restoration, the value moves not the shape" reading the maintainer accepted on #10954. ⚠️ If your measurement shows any consumer keying on the **absence** of `primaryKey`, that reading is wrong — stop and report rather than shipping it.
- serial constraint: `packages/services/service-datasource`. Free.

## ⛔ Lane red line — this card names a file this lane does not own

The root cause spans two contracts, and **one of them is `packages/spec/src/contracts/schema-diff-service.ts:59`**. This lane has **zero `packages/spec` ownership**. Do not reconcile the two spellings by editing spec, and do not edit `packages/objectql/src/util.ts` either.

The card's own suggested fix is entirely inside this lane and that is the fix to build: read the seam defensively in `external-datasource-service.ts`. If you conclude the only correct repair is a spec change, **stop and report `needs_decision`** — do not reach into spec.

⚠️ Note the card's own ordering hint: it offers `col.primaryKey ?? col.isPrimary` and then says **"or better"** — fall back to `table.primaryKeys?.includes(col.name)`. Decide between them on measurement, and say which drivers you checked. A per-column flag and a table-level list can disagree (composite keys are the obvious case); say what happens then rather than assuming they never do.

## Re-derive the premise before fixing

The card was measured at framework `79ebb37`; the tree has moved. Confirm on current `origin/main` that the PK really is dropped, and confirm it **per driver** — the card claims "on **every** SQL driver (sqlite/postgres/mysql)". Do not inherit that claim; measure what you can and declare what you could not.

If the premise no longer holds, say so and stop. That is a valid outcome.

## The pin is the point of this card

The card explains precisely why the existing suite missed this:

> `external-datasource-service.test.ts` hand-writes its fake schema with `primaryKey: true` (the spec-contract spelling), so no test ever feeds it a real driver's `isPrimary` output.

So a pin that hand-writes the fixed spelling would reproduce the original blindness exactly. **Drive `generateObjectDraft` off a real `SqlDriver.introspectSchema()` result**, as the card asks. If your instrument makes that impractical, say so plainly rather than substituting a fake and calling it covered — and check whether the substitution would manufacture your desired conclusion (#10240's dev found exactly that about his own stub and fixed the instrument first).

Pin both directions:
- a table **with** a declared primary key yields `primaryKey: true` on the right field;
- a table **without** one still yields a draft and does not invent a key. An implementation that stamps `primaryKey: true` on the first column would pass a one-directional suite.

## Standing proof standard

- Ablation with the signature predicted **first**; restore proved byte-identical by `git hash-object` (print both hashes). State, argued from the files, whether a rebuild sits between edit and run, and prove `src/` vs `dist/` resolution. ⚠️ The card says the defect was "confirmed in the shipped `dist`" — so this package **has** a `dist/`, and the resolution question is live here, not theoretical.
- Zero-hit counter-check with a positive control on the same corpus. A non-zero from a term that pre-dates your change proves nothing either.
- Gate union derived on the **final** commit, clean tree, `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, **no path arguments**; exit codes captured before any pipe.
- Class #10309 is live — the derivation is known short by at least four mechanisms. Run the gates you judge relevant explicitly and say whether the derivation named them.
- Changeset required. Draft PR only — do not mark ready, arm auto-merge, or merge.
- Never `git stash`: the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- Do not report a grep hit count as a fact count.

## Refs

QA #10663 (parent) · #10712 (adjacent finding on the same object-draft output — `os build` fails on the generated object: missing `${namespace}_` prefix and no `sharingModel`. **Not in your scope**; if your work makes its fix obvious, put it in `notes_for_other_cards`.)

PM review. The catalog half lands (PR #11001 flipped ready, auto-merge armed); the object-draft half is escalated. Label moved to `needs-user-decision`, assignee cleared.

## The dispatch's stop condition fired, and the seat stopped

The claim comment said: *"if you find any consumer keying on the **absence** of `primaryKey`, that reasoning is wrong — stop and report instead of shipping it."* The strict schema **is** that consumer, and the seat found it and stopped rather than shipping a generator whose default output no longer compiles.

**Verified by content on `origin/main`, not accepted from the report:**

| claim | check | result |
|---|---|---|
| `fields.X.primaryKey` is not an authorable spec field key | grep `field.zod.ts` + `object.zod.ts` | **zero hits** |
| — and that zero is a real zero | positive control on the same corpus | `externalId` at `field.zod.ts:1406`, `.describe('Is external ID for upsert operations')` — the exact string quoted in the report |
| no alternative home in the binding block | read `object.zod.ts:1171` | `ObjectExternalBindingSchema = strictObject({…})` — **strict**, so an unknown key is rejected, not absorbed |

So the generator renders a key the platform's own compiler (`TS2353` against the `ServiceObject` annotation *the generator itself writes*) and its own validator (`unrecognized_keys` at `["fields","id"]`) both refuse — each measured with a same-program positive control showing the identical definition minus the key is clean.

⚠️ **And that is reachable today, without this PR.** `generateObjectDraft` already emits the key whenever the caller passes the `primaryKey` option, **and the existing suite pins that output** — so there is a pinned path producing a draft the platform refuses. Filed standalone as **#11000**; it is a defect regardless of how this card is routed.

## What landed, and why it is safe on its own

`refreshCatalog` was feeding `undefined` into `ExternalCatalogSchema`, whose `primaryKey` is `z.boolean().default(false)` — the default absorbed it silently, so the persisted `external_catalog` recorded **every column of every remote table** as not part of the remote key. Studio's schema browser and the boot gate read that record.

Clause-② stays **no** on this half, and the seat checked it rather than inheriting my assessment: on the catalog path the key is non-optional and always present, so no consumer keys on its absence. The shape does not change; the `true`s become true.

One judgement call worth a reviewer's eye, and the PR states it in the open rather than burying it: the helper reads the **union** of the three signals rather than a precedence chain, on the argument that no in-tree producer uses a `false` to negate a key another asserts. Today the question is moot — `SqlDriver` derives `isPrimary` **from** `primaryKeys`, so they cannot disagree — and the three staged-disagreement cases are labelled as hand-built for exactly that reason. If a reviewer thinks over-reporting is the worse failure, that is the line to argue.

## The card's "every SQL driver" claim — split, correctly

The seat did not inherit it, and the distinction it drew is the right one:

- **Supported for all dialects**, by code path plus one executed dialect: the `isPrimary` assignment is a **single dialect-independent site** in `introspectSchema`, downstream of the per-dialect `introspectPrimaryKeys`. The *spelling* collision cannot vary by dialect.
- **Not supported**: any per-dialect claim about the *content* of `primaryKeys`. Only SQLite was executed; Postgres and MySQL were read, not run, with no server reachable.

That is a stronger result than a dialect sweep would have given for this seam, and it is honest about the half it does not cover.

## ⛔ Maintainer decision — where does a federated object declare its remote primary key?

I am not ruling this, and the seat's own preference was explicitly contingent rather than confident. It turns on one fact neither of us established: **does anything in the runtime address or upsert a federated external record by a declared remote key today, or does it address by the object's own id?**

| | option | my read |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | emit `fields.X.primaryKey` anyway, as this card literally asks | ⛔ **I recommend against, and would push back if ruled.** It makes the QA clause's two halves — draft is *compilable* and carries the introspected PK — mutually exclusive, and ships codegen whose **default** output fails the platform's own validator. Emitted-by-default invalid metadata is strictly worse than today's silent drop for an AI author, because it teaches that the key is legal |
| **B** | reuse `fields.X.externalId` | ⛔ recommend against **unless** someone names a live consumer. The seat scanned and found none reading a *field's* `externalId` — the hits are SCIM, the batch API, and seed/mapping `upsertKey` aliases, which take a field **name** at dataset level. Routing a real value into an inert key buys the appearance of a fix. Maps badly onto composite keys |
| **C** | add an authorable spelling (e.g. `external.primaryKey: string[]`) | architecturally right, handles composite keys natively, declared = enforced. Cost: new `packages/spec` surface — **and this lane has zero spec ownership**, so it would carve like #10999 did |
| **D** | rule that the draft correctly omits it; this PR is the whole repair | defensible **if** nothing consumes a federated PK at runtime. `external_catalog` — which Studio and the boot gate actually read — already has a real `primaryKey` key and is fixed by #11001 |

**My recommendation: D now, C when a consumer appears** — and I would not spend the spec surface before that consumer exists. If someone can name a live consumer, it is C and the spec slice routes out of this lane. Either way #11000 needs fixing on its own, because the pinned invalid-output path exists today.

Say which and I dispatch it without further consultation.

## Three findings this run filed rather than absorbed

- **#10997** — SQLite introspection returns only the **first** column of a composite key: `introspectPrimaryKeys` filters `PRAGMA table_info` on `row.pk === 1`, but SQLite numbers members `1, 2, 3…`. Measured on a real composite table. Both output signals are wrong *together* (because `isPrimary` is derived from `primaryKeys`), so a consumer cannot recover the missing member by cross-checking. `SqliteWasmDriver` inherits it.
- **#10998** — `introspectSchema()` returns only `{ tables }`; the contract's `dialect` and its **required** `introspectedAt` are never emitted. Consequence: `suggestFieldTypeForSqlType` runs with `dialect` undefined on the whole federation path, and `refreshCatalog` persists `dialect: undefined`. Same two-contract collision as this card, a different column of it.
- **#11000** — the unauthorable draft key, above.

## One process defect of mine, recorded

The seat flagged that my dispatch's "first line must be the literal text `os-dev-report`" **conflicts with the standing dev contract** that the terminal message is JSON and nothing else. It followed the dispatch, emitted both, and said so rather than silently picking one — the right call. The instruction exists because the HTML-comment marker is eaten by the sanitizer (measured 5×), but I introduced the conflict and did not flag it. Mine to reconcile, not the seat's.

## Maintainer ruling recorded — **the driver aligns to the spec contract** (`packages/spec` is the one contract)

Provenance: maintainer, 2026-08-22, live session (「同意所有」, item 9 = 驱动侧对齐 spec 契约).
